name: Scout Hull
life: “I still remember getting my first room over a surf shop.” People around Juniper Street know Scout by a small Thursday habit. Scout knows which of the west-side porches has a seat in the shade.
voice: I rented a room through September and my final lifeguard check comes in August.
appearance: Scout has a loose dark braid, a heart-shaped face and prominent ears, and a favorite piece of clothing, a cropped bottle-green coat. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Scout listens with the head tilted a little to the left.
personality: Scout treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To cover the last three weeks of the room rental.
family: Ruben King is Scout’s cousin. Scout picks the meeting place. Ruben sets the time to leave. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *The understudy sings*, Ruben says, “I spent my student loan on a ticket to hear the original singer.”
connections: Levi Boyd (hotel employer). An early last paycheck has the hotel manager reconsidering where a retention bonus belongs.

reactions.situation: A visitor demands a refund after the season ends early
reactions.response: Scout checks the actual dates printed on the booking before discussing its refund.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Scout offers an ordinary errand that lets the distressed person leave without being followed by an audience.
